'''Martin Goldstern''' (born 7 May 1963 in Austria) is an Austrian mathematician and university professor<ref name="prof">{{cite web
 |url=https://tiss.tuwien.ac.at/mbl/blatt_struktur/anzeigen/10449
 |title=TU Wien Mitteilungsblatt 10/2021
 |access-date=2021-03-04}}</ref> for [[set theory]] at the [[TU Wien]] and head of the [https://dmg.tuwien.ac.at/fb8/ST.html research unit 8] of the [https://dmg.tuwien.ac.at/ Institute of Discrete Mathematics and Geometry].<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://tiss.tuwien.ac.at/person/139798.html
 |title=Goldstern's TU Wien directory entry 
 |access-date=2023-12-14}}</ref>
His main research lies in [[set theory of the real line]] and [[forcing (mathematics)|forcing theory]], and applications of set theory in [[universal algebra]].

He is cousin of [[Martin Karplus]] and great-nephew of [[Eugenie Goldstern]].<ref>{{cite web
 |url=http://dmg.tuwien.ac.at/goldstern/www/
 |title=Goldstern's TU Wien home page
 |access-date=2023-12-14}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
 |url=http://www.hohenemsgenealogie.at/gen/getperson.php?personID=I12254
 |website=Hohenems Genealogie
 |title=Familienblatt Goldstern
 |access-date=2021-02-01}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Goldstern earned a Ph.D. in 1986<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://www.tuwien.at/en/studies/studying-at-tu-wien/promotio-sub-auspiciis
 |title=TU Wien list of Phd graduates ''sub auspiciis praesidentis''
 |access-date=2021-01-04}}</ref>  at the [[TU Wien]] under the direction of [[Robert F. Tichy]],<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=27218
 |title=Tichy's mathgenealogy entry
 |access-date=2021-01-04}}</ref> with a dissertation in equidistribution;<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://permalink.catalogplus.tuwien.at/AC00235421
 |title=TU Wien library entry for Goldstern's dissertation
 |access-date=2021-03-04}}</ref> and another in set theory in 1991 at [[UC Berkeley]]<ref>{{cite thesis
 |url=http://oskicat.berkeley.edu/record=b14691341~S1
 |title=UC Berkeley library entry for Goldstern's dissertation
 |year=1991
 |access-date=2021-03-04|last1=Goldstern
 |first1=Martin Robert
 }}</ref> under the direction of [[Jack Silver]] and Haim Judah. As postdoc he held temporary positions at [[Bar Ilan University]], [[Freie Universität Berlin]] and [[Carnegie Mellon University]]. He acquired [[habilitation]] at TU Wien in 1993<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://tiss.tuwien.ac.at/mbl/blatt_struktur/anzeigen/7137
 |title=TU Wien Mitteilungsblatt 12/1994
 |access-date=2021-03-04}}</ref> with the thesis 
''Tools for your forcing construction'', which greatly simplified, and made widely accessible, a general preservation theorem of [[Saharon Shelah]] for countable support [[proper forcing]] iterations. 
In 1993 he started working at TU Wien, where he is now full professor.<ref name="prof"/>

In 1996, Goldstern won the [[Prize of the Austrian Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oemg.ac.at/Preise.html|title=List of prize recipients, ÖMG|access-date=2021-01-04}}</ref>
In 2015,   2018 and 2023 he held visiting professor positions at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].
Together with Jakob Kellner and Shelah he showed the consistency (assuming [[large cardinal]]s) of Cichoń's maximum, i.e., the statement that the ten "independent" entries in [[Cichoń's diagram]] are all different.
